_note: Locale -> plural rule family. Single source of truth for grammatical number: PluralRules.java reads it at class init, scripts/localization/validate-locale.py reads it to derive each locale's legal key set. Keys are the 2-letter prefix of the locale code, matching LocaleNumberWords.forLocale (note 'fi' is Filipino/fil_ph here, not Finnish - Dungeon Train ships no Finnish). Families are implemented in both PluralRules.java and validate-locale.py; adding a locale here needs no code change, adding a FAMILY needs both.

_families.zero_one_other: one: n == 0 or n == 1; other: everything else (French, Portuguese)
_families.east_slavic: one: n%10 == 1 and n%100 != 11; few: n%10 in 2..4 and n%100 not in 12..14; many: everything else
_families.polish: one: n == 1; few: n%10 in 2..4 and n%100 not in 12..14; many: everything else
_families.romanian: one: n == 1; few: n == 0 or n%100 in 2..19; other: everything else (20 up, where the noun takes 'de')
_families.single: other: always - the language does not inflect for number
